plant.cvs: 'Midnight Rose Select' – denser pink speckling · 'Palace Purple' – plain bronze-purple, larger · 'Obsidian' – glossy near-black, no speckles · 'Plum Pudding' – plum with silver sheen
plant.foliage: evergreen; rounded lobed leaves, deep purple-black with pink speckles
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy in all of the UK including very cold winters, approximately -20 to -15°C.
plant.prune: Remove tatty or scorched leaves in spring and cut spent flower stems. Lift and divide every 3–4 years when crowns turn woody.
plant.resilience: Tough evergreen mound; leaf colour is best in light shade. Crowns lift and go woody with age. Pests: vine weevil grubs (especially in pots), occasional rust.
plant.soilWarning: Waterlogged winter soil rots the crown
sources: General knowledge of Heuchera hybrids and the Terra Nova 'Midnight Rose' description, as remembered, not checked online
RHS Heuchera growing guidance, as remembered, not checked online
ASPCA plant toxicity listing for Heuchera, as remembered, not checked online
uncertain: hardiness: RHS band not confirmed. H6 is a judgement from the hardiness of Heuchera hybrids in general, and the RHS may list it as H7. Check before printing.
height and spread: approximate. The foliage mound is about 25 cm and flower stems reach about 40–45 cm. The breeder's figures were not checked.
compliance: this is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction and may carry UK/EU plant breeders' rights. No grant number is known, so the field is left blank.
clay: left blank. Heucheras dislike heavy wet clay but cope with improved clay, and I can't give a firm yes or no.
hue: dark plum-purple judged at about 300. The pink speckling shifts the effect.
peak: given as a foliage band Apr-Oct because the plant is evergreen and sold on its leaves. The flowering months (roughly May-Jul) were not verified.
sunMin: estimated. The plant tolerates fairly deep shade, but leaf colour dulls there.
cvs: 'Midnight Rose Select' is named from memory as a sport with more speckling. Verify it exists in UK trade.
toxicity: Heuchera is not known to be toxic and is listed non-toxic to cats and dogs by the ASPCA as remembered. This was not checked online.
plant.uses: Front of border · containers · woodland edge · ground cover · foliage contrast
plant.visual: Near-black purple leaves speckled hot pink, speckles ageing paler · evergreen mound · airy sprays of small pinkish flowers in early summer
plant.water: Water regularly in the first summer and in dry spells; keep pots evenly moist but never sitting wet.
